summary:
The M1 fix (O-019) is correct and tested, but I found one more gap that lets the parity check report AGREE over real drift.

**The fix.** It is in commit 0120c5f. Read-Entries in `eng/rules-parity.ps1` (lines 211-224) now skips blank lines and comment-only lines inside a `must_not_match` list. The list ends only at a line that is neither, indented no deeper than the key, and the loop still stops at the next entry or the settled marker. `RuleCases.ps1` C-005 gained four rows, each putting a yaml-only pattern after a gap: a blank line, a comment at the key's indent, a deeper comment, and a blank line plus a comment. Each must give DRIFT. A control row, a blank line and a comment between two real items, must still give AGREE. I read the tests and they feed those shapes in.

**What I re-ran on this tree:**
- Parity gives AGREE under both powershell.exe and pwsh (7 Facts, 10 twinned entries, 21 patterns, 7 settled).
- RuleCases C-001 to C-005: 8, 34, 26, 26 and 90 checks, none failing.
- RuleCopiesAgreeTests plus ArchitectureRulesTests: 8/8.
- Fitness: 17 rules hold.
- The full harness against the real engine: CLEAN, 32/32 rows AS-RECORDED, exit 0. That makes five runs with the same verdict for every row.
- `git status` was unchanged afterwards.

**The new gap (M2).** It is in the same reader, so I should have caught it in attempt 1. An entry opened by a bare `  -` line, with `name:` on the next line, is legal YAML. When it is the first entry after `rules:`, the reader never sees it. I checked this on a temp copy: such a yaml-only rule gave AGREE, exit 0, while `yaml.safe_load` read 18 rules. The same spelling later in the list makes a must_not_import entry pass without a word, even though the normal `  - name:` spelling of that entry gives CANNOT-READ.

**Stale statements.** Nothing else in the files I passed described the old stop-at-blank behaviour, so none are now false. The C-005 title was updated. The only change in behaviour is correct: a comment deeper than the key, which used to exit 2, is now skipped as YAML does.

findings.claim: The reader misses an entry opened by a bare dash line: `  -` with `name:` on the next line, which is legal YAML and which PyYAML, and so Fitness, reads as an entry. The entry scan only knows `^(\s*)-\s+name\s*:`, and its catch-all refusal `^  -\s` needs a character after the dash. A bare `  -` line therefore matches neither pattern and is never recognised as an entry. Two results, both checked on a temp copy. (a) As the first entry after `rules:`, a yaml-only rule in this form ('AYamlOnlyRule (*.cs)', must_not_match '(?m)OnlyInYaml') lies before any recognised entry and is never read: 'rules-parity: AGREE 7 facts <- 10 twinned entries, 21 patterns', exit 0, while yaml.safe_load reads 18 rules. (b) Further down the list, the entry is folded into the one before it. If it has a must_not_match, that gives a misleading 'two must_not_match keys' (exit 2). If it is a must_not_import rule, it gives AGREE, exit 0, where the same entry spelled `  - name:` gives 'has no must_not_match' (exit 2). This is the same consequence as M1: a rule Fitness enforces and xUnit does not gets past RuleCopiesAgreeTests. It is the C-003 shape ('a yaml entry above the settled marker with no Fact') in a spelling the reader neither reads nor refuses, which breaks the design's rule that both readers refuse any shape they cannot classify.
findings.evidence: eng/rules-parity.ps1:187-193. Line 188 is `if ($lines[$i] -cmatch '^(\s*)-\s+name\s*:')`. Line 192 is `elseif ($lines[$i] -cmatch '^  -\s') { Stop-Reading ... "an entry that does not start with 'name:'" }`. Lines are split on `\r?\n`, so a bare `  -` has nothing after the dash for `\s` to match. No case in tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1 (C-003 at 233-261, C-005 at 290-364) feeds this spelling.
findings.fix: At eng/rules-parity.ps1:192, change the refusal regex from '^  -\s' to '^  -(\s|$)', so a bare `  -` line anywhere in the list exits 2 with file:line. Add a C-005 (or C-003) row that puts a `  -` / `    name: ...` entry first after `rules:` and one before the settled marker, and requires CANNOT-READ under both powershell.exe and pwsh, never AGREE.

obligations.evidence: eng/rules-parity.ps1:211-224: `if ($line.Trim().Length -eq 0 -or $line -cmatch '^\s*#') { continue }` comes before the indent-based break, and the loop is bounded by `$end`. tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1:342-364 has the four hidden-pattern rows (each DRIFT 2 unpaired with "only in yaml 'OnlyInYaml'") and the AGREE control. C-005 gave 90 ok and 0 FAIL in my run under both shells. This closes the shapes M1 named. M2 is a separate entry-level shape.

drift: Nothing new departed from the design in attempt 2. The only change in behaviour: a comment line deeper than the key inside a must_not_match list used to exit 2 ('runs onto the next line') and is now skipped. That matches YAML's own reading and the design's intent that the reader agree with what Fitness reads.
